ui: SSD delivery is shown 10:30 AM–2:30 PM Monday–Saturday through Dec 26; backpack checks are scheduled after the latest child pickup in the first free slot, and stale morning reminders are repaired. Cleared project actions stay cleared, sync conflicts pause automatic overwrites for review, the Money account-exit checklist now uses working tap controls, Spirituality shortcuts keep consistent full-page navigation, and Money distinguishes linked accounts from budget-mapped accounts and separates balance dates from connection sync dates, and blocks confirmed-closed checking from available-cash mapping, and preserves subscription payment and renewal details across sync, and shows an estimated renewal separately from confirmed bills, and rejects generic bank fees as bill matches. Version reporting now uses one build identifier across startup, system health, and the update check. Budget now distinguishes no bills due this month from no bills saved, and the Accounts empty state explains when synced accounts still need Money mapping. Spirituality journal saves and daily-practice toggles now restore the previous state and show an error if the local save fails. Money now surfaces possible monthly charges from repeated posted transactions, labels them as estimates, and keeps them separate from saved bills and cash forecasts. The monthly-payment review also surfaces variable-amount patterns with observed ranges, while keeping all candidates outside confirmed bill totals. Build identifiers now share one source, service-worker cache versions follow the registered build, and cloud snapshot writes verify the live release before accepting data. Friday Dolly dance remains at 5:15 PM, Friday Dad pickup is corrected to about 4:30 PM, and the Nov 6 occurrence notes that Leo and Demitri were picked up Nov 5. On SSD driver delivery days, Daily Flow omits the home-from-UPS shower block and auto-scheduled home/school chores before and during the route; hydration reminders remain visible. Habit building is now available across the life areas: Today gathers active habits, each area page shows its own habits, and users can add, log, edit, pause, or resume habits. Practice history is saved in the existing local/cloud snapshot; appointments and one-time tasks remain separate. The Today all-area habit view is now the default starting page. Habit reminders can be enabled per habit as a timed 14-day phone-notification trial; reminders stop after the trial and skip days already logged. Growth & Hobbies now includes a 19-doll Monster High starter catalog with real product photos, generation/search/ownership filters for Michelle and Dolly, and a custom-doll form. The expanded catalog includes G3 Venus, alternate Venus releases, the Love in Scaris Garrott du Roque and Rochelle Goyle two-pack, and distinct Draculaura releases. Ownership selections sync in the existing snapshot. Family home now keeps vertical scrolling enabled on phones. The app update check now reads the shared APP_BUILD constant, and the service-worker asset list has valid JavaScript so the Monster High files install and refresh with the app. A visible Monster High dolls shortcut now appears in the Garden + Hobbies open-sections area, where it opens the collection tracker. The Hobby Projects drawer now has a dedicated Monster High collection card with an Open tracker button. The external archive button is removed from the tracker; doll browsing and custom entries stay in Daily Life. The Love in Scaris two-pack is now listed as separate Garrott du Roque and Rochelle Goyle cards with independent ownership checkboxes. The shared app shell now preserves vertical touch scrolling across phone pages, including Home, instead of limiting scrolling to selected views. Monster High ownership changes now wait for the local save and attempt an immediate guarded cloud snapshot push, avoiding a refresh race with the delayed background sync. Monster High collection sync now merges timestamped ownership from cloud and preserves the collection against older full-snapshot writes. Habit reminders now stay active until turned off instead of expiring after a 14-day trial; the server dispatcher accepts ongoing schedules. App updates now wait for a clear Reload now choice instead of force-reloading open tabs as soon as a new service worker installs; saved work stays available while an update waits. The offline app worker now keeps the current version if a required core file cannot download, and the update check blocks a release dated earlier than the installed build. The service worker now caches all current page scripts and stylesheets, including household maps and reading/task helpers, for more complete offline use. A small save-status strip now shows local, syncing, cloud-synced, offline, or review-needed state and opens Cloud settings. A one-tap Workday focus button shows today’s UPS/SSD route blocks and the next scheduled commitment without household chore lists. Workday focus now selects the next scheduled event rather than surfacing a chore as the next commitment. Habit check-ins are now reachable from a compact strip across the app, and saved task, water, habit, and Day Flow completions get a brief positive checkmark animation. Habit progress now appears in a compact check-in strip throughout the app, with Done and Partly actions, a daily progress bar, and a gentle saved-completion toast. The Monster High catalog now includes 10 additional releases with official Mattel product photos, bringing the starter list to 32, with Toralei Stripe Creeproduction and Sweet Screams Twyla. Hobby project cards have separate Start, Finish, Resume, and Restart controls. The Hobbies workspace has one-tap project starters for beginner yoga, a first kombucha batch, and crafting; they create editable project drafts only when Michelle chooses to save them. Hobby projects now have separate Start, Finish, Resume, and Restart controls for quick progress updates. Monster High catalog navigation now loads after the expanded entries were corrected.
